:::{#exm-negate-quantifiers}
#### Negating "every integer is even"
<!-- no-figure: a rewording of one sentence; nothing to plot -->

Let $S$ be the [integers](number-systems.qmd#def-integers),
and let $P(x)$ be "$x$ is [even](number-systems.qmd#def-even-odd)".
By [De Morgan's law for a universal quantifier](#thm-negate-quantifiers),
$\neg (\forall x \in S, P(x)) \equiv \exists x \in S, \neg P(x)$:
the [negation](#def-not) of "every [integer](number-systems.qmd#def-integers) is even"
is "some integer is not even".
By [De Morgan's law for an existential quantifier](#thm-negate-existential),
$\neg (\exists x \in S, P(x)) \equiv \forall x \in S, \neg P(x)$:
the negation of "some integer is even"
is "no integer is even".

:::
